title: Digital Skills for Study and Work
summary: Manage files, cloud storage, email and notes, search and judge sources, avoid plagiarism, and take part in video calls with confidence on any device.
audience: Secondary and university students who use a phone, tablet or computer for study

lessons.title: Files and folders on phone, tablet and computer

body.p: Everything you save on a device is a file: an essay, a photo, a voice note, a PDF of past questions. Files are kept in folders, which work like labelled boxes. Folders can hold other folders, so you can build a tree. The idea is the same on a phone, a tablet and a computer, although the app is called something different, such as Files, My Files or File Explorer.

Every file has a name and an extension, which is the short ending after the dot. The extension tells the device which app should open the file. Common ones are .docx or .odt for documents, .pdf for fixed-layout documents, .xlsx or .csv for spreadsheets, .jpg or .png for pictures, and .mp3 or .mp4 for audio and video. Do not delete or change the extension when you rename a file, or it may stop opening.

body.h: Name files so you can find them later

body.p: Names such as 'essay final NEW (2)' or 'IMG_4821' are useless after a month. A good name says what the file is, and starting with the date in year-month-day order makes files sort in time order automatically.

body.code:
Poor:   final final NEW (2).docx
Poor:   IMG_4821.jpg
Good:   2026-10-07_Biology_Essay_v2.docx
Good:   2026-09-15_Chemistry_Notes_Acids.pdf

School
  Year 11
    Biology
    Chemistry
    Mathematics
  Scholarship applications
  Certificates and IDs

steps: Make one main folder for school or study, then one folder for each year or term.
Inside it, make a folder for each subject.
Move files into the right folder as soon as you download them. Check the Downloads folder weekly, because that is where files collect.
Delete duplicates and old drafts, but keep the latest version.
Keep a second copy of important files, such as certificates, somewhere else (see the next lesson).

body.tip: On a shared or borrowed phone, files you download may land in a folder other people can browse. Do not store ID scans or passwords on a device you do not control.

lessons.title: Cloud storage and sharing files safely

body.p: Cloud storage means files kept on a company's computers on the internet, which you reach with an account and a password. You can open the same file on a phone, a tablet and a computer. Most services give a limited amount of free space and charge for more. If your phone is lost, broken or stolen, files that are in the cloud are still safe, which is the main reason to use it.

Syncing keeps copies on your device and in the cloud matching. That also means that if you delete or damage a file on one device, the change usually copies to the others. Most services keep deleted files in a bin or trash for a limited time, so check there quickly if you delete by mistake. A real backup is a separate copy that does not change when the original changes, for example important files copied to both the cloud and a memory stick.

Uploading uses mobile data, which is costly for many learners. Set your phone to upload only on Wi-Fi. Photos are large: 250 photos of about 3 MB each take about 250 x 3 = 750 MB. Before you upload, delete blurry shots and duplicates. You can also make files available offline before you leave a place with Wi-Fi, so you can open them later without data.

list: Viewer: can read but not change.
Commenter: can read and add comments, which is ideal for feedback on a draft.
Editor: can change the file, so give it only to people you trust, such as members of your project group.

body.p: You can share with named people by email address, or create a link. A link that 'anyone with the link' can open is convenient, but anyone who gets the link, even through a forwarded message, can open it. Use named people for anything personal, such as a CV with your phone number, a scanned ID or exam results.

steps: Open the sharing option for the file or folder.
Add the email addresses of the people who need access.
Choose the lowest permission that does the job: viewer, commenter or editor.
Send them the link and check that it opens for them.
When the project ends, remove access you no longer need.

body.tip: Protect your account with a long, unique password and two-step verification, where a code is sent to your phone when you sign in. If someone gets into your cloud account, they get all your files.

body.p: Email is still the main way that schools, universities, employers and scholarship offices communicate. A professional email has a clear subject line, a greeting, a short message, a polite ending and your name. Write it so a busy person understands what you want in ten seconds.

body.code:
To: ms.adeyemi@example.org
Subject: Biology project - request for deadline extension

Dear Ms Adeyemi,

I am Kemi Bello from Class 11B. I was ill last week and have a doctor's note. May I submit the Biology project on Friday instead of Wednesday?

Thank you for your time.

Yours sincerely,
Kemi Bello

body.h: To, Cc, Bcc and Reply all

list: To: the people who must act.
Cc: people who should know, but need not act.
Bcc: hidden recipients. Use it when sending to a large group so that people's addresses are not exposed.
Reply goes only to the sender. Reply all goes to everyone on the message, so use it only when everyone needs your answer. If a teacher emails 120 students, replying to all fills 120 inboxes.

body.p: An attachment is a file sent with the email. Email services limit the total size, and the limit varies, so check yours. Suppose your limit is 25 MB and you want to send five photos of 4 MB each (5 x 4 = 20 MB) and a 7 MB PDF. The total is 20 + 7 = 27 MB, which is over the limit. Options: reduce the photo size, send fewer files in each message, or upload the files to cloud storage and send a link. Always mention the attachment in your message and check that you attached the right, final version.

Phishing is a message that pretends to be a bank, a school, a mobile money service or a scholarship to trick you into giving a password, a PIN or money. Warning signs include urgency ('act in one hour'), threats, spelling mistakes, an address that does not match the organisation, and a request to enter your password through a link. Do not click. Open the official app or type the website address yourself, or phone the organisation using a number you already know. No genuine organisation should ask for your full PIN or password by email.

body.tip: If a scholarship asks you to pay a fee through a personal account before you can be considered, treat it as a warning and check with the awarding body directly.

body.p: Typing a whole question into a search engine often works, but you will get better results if you think about keywords. Pick the two to four most important words and leave out filler words. 'How does the water cycle work in geography for class 9' becomes 'water cycle stages diagram'. If results are poor, change one word at a time.

list: Quotation marks find an exact phrase: "causes of the First World War" only shows pages with those words together in that order.
A minus sign removes a word: jaguar -car helps if you want the animal.
site: limits results to one website or type of address, such as site:gov.uk education.
filetype:pdf finds documents in a particular format, such as past papers in PDF form.
Most major search engines support these. Some small differences may exist, so test them.

body.p: Results marked 'Ad' or 'Sponsored' are paid for. They are not necessarily false, but they are there because someone paid. Also remember that being at the top of the list does not prove that a page is true; it only means the engine thought it matched your search.

steps: Who wrote it? Look for a named author or an organisation with real expertise and contact details.
What is the purpose? Information, selling something, entertainment or persuasion?
What is the evidence? Reliable pages name their sources, so you can check them.
When was it written? Information on laws, prices, health advice and technology goes out of date.
Do other independent sources agree? Open new tabs and see what other trusted sites say.

body.p: Checking other sources is called lateral reading, and it is more powerful than studying the page itself, because anyone can make a professional-looking website. Web address endings give clues: government or university addresses such as gov.uk, gov.ng, gov.gh, go.ke or ac.uk are usually official. But an ending alone is never proof, so still check the author and date. Be extra careful with screenshots, forwarded messages and videos, which can be edited or taken out of context. Search for the original source before sharing.

body.tip: For homework, use more than one source, and write down where each fact came from as you go. That saves you from hunting later for your references.

lessons.title: Copy and paste, plagiarism and basic referencing

body.p: Copying and pasting is a useful tool for moving your own text, quotes and data. It becomes plagiarism when you present someone else's words or ideas as your own. Plagiarism is taken seriously at schools, universities and examination bodies, and it can lead to lost marks, cancelled results or worse. The good news is that it is simple to avoid.

body.h: Three ways to use someone else's work honestly

list: Quote: copy the exact words, put them in quotation marks and give the source. Use short quotes only.
Paraphrase: put the idea in your own words and sentence structure, and still give the source. Changing three or four words in a copied sentence is not paraphrasing.
Summarise: give the main points of a longer text in a few sentences of your own, with the source.

body.p: The same rule applies to pictures, data tables, music and code. Ideas also need credit: you may write every word yourself and still need a reference if the idea is not yours. If you use an AI writing tool, follow your school's rules about whether and how you must say so. Handing in text you did not write as your own work is dishonest whichever tool produced it.

A reference lets your reader find the source you used. Different schools and universities use different styles, such as Harvard, APA or MLA, so use the one your teacher asks for. The basic ingredients are always similar: who made it (author or organisation), the year, the title, the publisher or website name, and for web pages the address and the date you looked at it.

body.code:
In the text:   Plants lose water through their leaves (Okafor, 2022).

Reference list:
Okafor, C. (2022) Introduction to plant biology. Lagos: Example Press.

Web page:
Example Weather Service (2025) How rain forms. Available at: https://example.org/rain (Accessed: 7 October 2026).

body.p: The names above are invented to show the pattern. Copy the layout your own style guide gives, and be consistent: the same order, punctuation and capital letters for every reference.

steps: Note the author, date, title and web address while you read, not afterwards.
Put quotation marks around any words you copy straight into your notes.
Write your own version of each idea in your draft.
Add the citation in the text where you use the idea.
Finish with a reference list, in alphabetical order if your style requires it.

body.tip: A good test: if your teacher asked 'Where did you get this?', could you show them? If not, you need a reference.

lessons.title: Video calls, online behaviour and time zones

body.p: Classes, interviews, tutoring and study groups often happen over video calls. A little preparation avoids most problems. Netiquette means good manners online. The basic rule is the same as face to face: show respect and think about how your words will be received.

list: Join a few minutes early and test your sound. Headphones usually reduce echo and background noise.
Charge your device or plug it in, and close other apps that use data.

Choose a quiet place with light in front of you, not behind you. If your connection is weak, turn off your camera or lower the video quality so the sound stays clear. Audio-only is fine when the teacher agrees.
Know the day, time and time zone, and check the link in advance.
Stay muted when you are not speaking and unmute to talk.
Use the hand-raise button or the chat to ask a question without interrupting.
Do not record or take screenshots of other people unless everyone has agreed. Many schools have rules on this.
Dress and behave as you would for class. Remember the chat is part of the record.
Be careful with background items and private information on your screen.

body.p: When a group is spread across countries, agree a time clearly. Nigeria uses UTC+1, Ghana, Sierra Leone and The Gambia use UTC+0, Zambia UTC+2 and Kenya UTC+3, and these countries do not change their clocks in summer. A call at 14:00 in Lagos is 14 - 1 = 13:00 UTC, which is 13:00 in Accra, 15:00 in Lusaka and 16:00 in Nairobi. The UK, Ireland, Spain and Canada move their clocks forward and back during the year, so for them check the date with a world clock tool. Always write the time zone next to the time.

Keep messages short and polite. Writing in capital letters feels like shouting. Read your message before sending, because tone is hard to hear in text. If you are angry, wait before replying. Never share another person's photo or private message without their permission.

body.tip: A chat message you send in anger can be screenshotted and shared. Pause first.

lessons.title: Digital notes and simple document formatting

body.p: Digital notes are searchable, easy to back up and easy to reorganise, but only if they are organised in the first place. A phone full of unlabelled screenshots of the blackboard is hard to revise from. Choose one notes app or one folder system and use it for every subject.

list: One notebook or folder for each subject, and one note for each topic or lesson.
Give each note a clear title and the date: '2026-10-07 Chemistry - Acids and bases'.
Use headings and bullet lists, not one long block of text.
Add tags or keywords such as 'exam' or 'to review' so you can find things with search.
If you photograph handwritten notes or a board, crop the picture, name it and file it with the topic.
Back up your notes, for example by syncing them to the cloud and exporting important ones as PDF files.

body.p: After a lesson, spend five minutes cleaning up. Write a two-line summary at the top and list any questions you still have. Searching is quick only if you used words you will remember later.
A well-formatted assignment is easier to read and can earn better marks. Word processors in every tool have the same core features. Use them rather than doing things by hand.

steps: Use Heading styles for headings, instead of just making text big and bold. Styles let the program build a table of contents and help screen readers.
Choose one clear font in a readable size (11 or 12 points is common) and use it throughout.
Use the line spacing and margins your teacher asks for. Do not press Enter several times to move to a new page; insert a page break.
Use the bullet and number buttons for lists. Never line things up with the space bar; use a tab or a table.
Add page numbers, then proofread and run the spell-checker with the correct language setting, for example British English.
Save the final version, and export it as a PDF if you are sending it to someone, so the layout stays the same on any device.

body.tip: Save often and keep versions: v1, v2, final. If your phone battery dies or the app crashes, you will lose less. Turn on autosave if your app has it.

quiz.q: Which file name will still make sense in a year and sort neatly with other files?
options: essay final NEW (2) - copy (1).docx
IMG_4821 final final (1) latest.docx
biology essay latest one again.docx
2026-10-07_Biology_Essay_v2.docx

quiz.q: You must send an essay to a teacher who uses a different device. How can you best keep the layout exactly as you made it?
options: Export it as a PDF so the layout stays fixed
Send a screenshot of the first page only
Rename the file with a longer, clearer name
Delete the file extension so any app opens it

quiz.q: Your email limit is 25 MB. You want to attach five photos of 4 MB each and a 7 MB PDF. What is the best action?
options: The total is 20 MB, under the limit, so everything will fit easily
The total is 27 MB, but email services accept any size anyway
The total is 27 MB, over the limit, so send a cloud link instead
Attach each photo twice, so a copy arrives if one fails

quiz.q: Nasra deletes a file from a synced folder on her laptop. What is most likely to happen?
options: Nothing changes on her other devices, because each one keeps its own copy
It is deleted on her other devices too, though the bin may keep it for a while
The file stays safe on every device, since syncing only adds new files
The cloud company phones her to confirm before anything is removed

quiz.q: A group project file should let classmates leave feedback but not change your text. Which permission should you give?
options: Editor, so they can leave notes and fix mistakes
Owner, so they can leave notes and manage sharing
Commenter, so they can leave notes but not edit
No permission, but send the file by email only

quiz.q: Which sharing setting is the riskiest for a file containing your ID scan and phone number?
options: Shared with one named person, who can only view it
Anyone with the link can open it, with no sign-in
Kept private, so only your own account can open it
Shared with a named teacher, who can only comment

quiz.q: An email says 'Your account will close in one hour. Click here and enter your password.' What should you do?
options: Do not click; go to the official app or site yourself, or phone them
Click quickly and enter your password before the hour runs out
Forward it to your friends with the link as a warning to them
Reply with your password so that they can confirm it is yours

quiz.q: A teacher emails 120 students to ask who can attend a trip. You cannot go. What is the best reply?
options: Reply all, so every student sees that you cannot go
Forward it to a friend and ask them to answer for you
Say nothing, since the teacher will assume you cannot come
Reply to the teacher only, saying you cannot come

quiz.q: You want pages that contain the exact phrase "causes of the First World War" in that order. What should you do?
options: Put a minus sign in front of the whole phrase
Put the whole phrase inside quotation marks
Type it in capital letters so it matches exactly
Add the word 'ad' at the end of the phrase

quiz.q: You find a surprising claim on a website you do not know. Which action is most useful?
options: Check other tabs for independent, trusted sources saying the same
Check whether the site looks professional and has a modern design
Share it with friends first and check whether it is true later
Trust it because it appeared as the first search result on the page

quiz.q: A page on a smartphone buying guide was written many years ago. Why does the date matter?
options: Older pages are wrong about everything, so they should be ignored
The date only affects the colour and layout of the page shown
A date means the page has been checked and approved by a government
Prices, models and advice change, so the page may be out of date

quiz.q: A student copies a paragraph, changes three words and adds no source. How should this be described?
options: Paraphrasing, because three words were changed to make it new
Fine, because information on the web is free for anyone to copy
Plagiarism, because the words are mostly copied and no source is given
A summary, because the student shortened the original paragraph

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of a reference list?
options: To let readers find and check the sources you used
To make the essay look longer and add pages to it
To show readers which font and page layout you used
To replace the need to write your own ideas in it

quiz.q: A call is at 14:00 in Lagos (UTC+1). What time is it in Nairobi (UTC+3)?
You join a video lesson from a noisy home. What is the best habit?
options: Stay unmuted so the teacher hears all the background sounds too
Stay muted until you speak and use the chat or hand-raise to ask
Record the other students for fun and share it without asking them
Turn up the volume on your speakers to the maximum so you hear better

quiz.q: You are making a long assignment. Why is it better to use heading styles than to make text big and bold by hand?
options: Heading styles make the file smaller than any other formatting
Hand formatting is not allowed in most word processors or schools
The program can then build a table of contents and navigate by headings
Heading styles change the document into a PDF when you save it
